security_audit.summary: All 57 static findings are false positives. remediation.issue: The documentation includes an author-specific absolute local path.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the absolute path with a project-relative path such as recipes.js before publishing.

content.value_statement: Recipe data can become inconsistent when entries use different fields or formats. This skill provides a clear schema, validation checklist, and conversion guidance for CookMode V2 recipes.
actual_capabilities: Creates recipe entries using the documented CookMode V2 object structure.
Edits recipe names, categories, components, ingredients, instructions, notes, and image URL fields.
Checks required fields, ingredient shapes, category values, and JavaScript formatting.
Converts ingredient strings into amount, unit, ingredient, and optional prep fields.
Explains how recipe scaling and display formatting work in the documented examples.
limitations: It documents one CookMode V2 recipe schema and may not match other applications.
It does not fetch recipes, verify image availability, or validate external URL content.
It cannot determine food safety, nutrition, allergens, or cooking quality.
It relies on the user to provide the target recipes.js file and project conventions.

use_cases.title: Add a structured recipe
use_cases.description: Create a new recipe entry with components, ingredient objects, and ordered instructions.
use_cases.target_user: Home cook maintaining a CookMode V2 collection

use_cases.title: Normalize imported recipes
use_cases.description: Convert copied ingredient lines into the object fields required by recipes.js.

use_cases.title: Review recipe consistency
use_cases.description: Check an edited recipe against the documented schema before adding it to the collection.
use_cases.target_user: Developer maintaining the CookMode V2 application

prompt_templates.title: Create a recipe
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a CookMode V2 recipe entry for chocolate chip cookies. Use the documented object schema and include ingredients, instructions, and notes.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a recipe entry
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this CookMode V2 recipe entry. List missing or invalid fields, then provide a corrected version that follows the documented schema. [Paste entry]

prompt_templates.title: Convert ingredients
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these ingredient lines into CookMode V2 ingredient objects with amount, unit, ingredient, and prep fields when available. [Paste ingredients]

prompt_templates.title: Validate a batch update
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these edited CookMode V2 recipes with the documented schema. Identify inconsistent categories, invalid ingredient objects, and formatting issues. Return a prioritized correction list. [Paste entries]

output_examples.input: Create a recipe entry for tomato soup.
output: An Entree, Side, Soup, or Dessert category.
Ingredient objects grouped under a component.
Ordered preparation instructions and optional notes.

output_examples.input: Convert “2 cups flour, sifted” to the structured format.
output_examples.output: An ingredient object with amount 2, unit cups, ingredient all-purpose flour, and prep sifted.

output: A list of missing required fields.
Warnings for empty ingredient values or invalid categories.
A concise set of recommended corrections.

best_practices: Follow the existing recipes.js style before adding or changing entries.
Use clear component names and explicit units for every ingredient.
Review the validation checklist after each edit, especially for imported recipes.
anti_patterns: Do not use free-form ingredient strings when the application expects ingredient objects.
Do not add categories outside the documented Entree, Side, Soup, and Dessert values.
Do not treat image URLs as verified unless you check them outside this skill.

faq.question: What file does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It is designed for recipe data stored in recipes.js for CookMode V2.

faq.question: Which recipe categories are supported?
faq.answer: The documented categories are Entree, Side, Soup, and Dessert.

faq.question: Can it convert copied recipe text?
faq.answer: Yes. It can convert ingredient lines into structured ingredient objects when quantities and units are available.

faq.question: Are notes required?
faq.answer: No. Notes are optional and can be a single string or an array of strings.

faq.question: Can it check image links?
faq.answer: It can check that a field has a URL-like value, but it does not verify that the image is reachable or safe.

faq.question: Does it edit files automatically?
faq.answer: The skill provides instructions and validation guidance. File changes depend on the AI tool and user approval workflow.
